title: Xanthe and the Current
premise: When a government survey team vanishes above the Kestrel Narrows, riverboat captain Sable Reyes is the only pilot willing to run the glacial reach before calving season seals it. Racing a salvage fleet that wants the survey's find buried, she discovers the vanished team was mapping a drowned pre-dam town—and that the lead surveyor is the sister whose death she's spent twelve years outrunning. To save the one survivor and expose what the fleet's backer will kill to hide, Sable must finally claim the name and the past she buried. The book ends with her testimony forcing the salvage operation's collapse, the wreck protected, and Sable choosing to captain her own route rather than disappear again.
about_author: Sable Yarrow is a former deckhand on inland waterways who now writes adventure fiction from a houseboat on the northern rivers. Her work draws on a decade of hauling freight through seasonal channels and the people who live by the water's moods.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Establishes her life aboard the riverboat Marrow: running cargo, reading sandbars, keeping no fixed address. A routine delivery upriver introduces her quiet competence and her rule of never taking passengers. Emotional beat: contentment with a hairline crack—she counts miles because years would demand accounting.

chapters.title: Gear and No Tracks
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A ranger hires her to ferry investigators to the survey team's last camp: tents standing, instruments running, coffee cold, and not a footprint leaving the mud. Sable reads the river signs better than the investigators and spots what they miss—a boat hauled into the willows, deliberately hidden. Beat: unease hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Salvage Fleet
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Three industrial salvage barges arrive at the landing, heavy with crane gear and men who don't answer questions. Their foreman, Corven Hale, offers Sable a contract to pilot them upriver—an offer with the texture of a threat. Beat: she recognizes power when it smiles, and declines carefully.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, with a dispatch from the hydrology office. The glacier above the Narrows will calve soon, opening the route for roughly six tides before ice closes it until spring. Whoever reaches the wreck site first holds it. Sable calculates her boat's speed against the fleet's and realizes she can't win by running—only by knowing water they don't. Beat: the gambler's cold clarity.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, flashback woven through a night anchorage. Twelve years ago she piloted under another name, and a survey run she captained ended with her sister drowned and Sable's license revoked on falsified findings. She buried the name and bought the Marrow. Beat: grief surfacing as anger at being dragged back toward the same water.

chapters.title: The Hidden Boat
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Following the hidden skiff's drag marks, she finds a survivor—junior surveyor Ilsa Voss—feverish and hiding in an abandoned fish camp. Ilsa won't say who she's hiding from, only that the survey team split over what the sonar found. Beat: reluctant responsibility; Sable's no-passengers rule breaks.

chapters.title: The Drowned Town
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV, fever-dream and memory. The sonar mapped Kettle Landing, a town flooded by the old dam project, its records sealed because the government flooded it with people still refusing to leave. The survey's lead, Dr. Ansen, was going public. Ilsa fled when Ansen's own crew turned. Beat: the scale of the secret revealed.

chapters.title: Hale's Second Offer
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Hale corners her at the fuel dock: he knows who she used to be, knows about the falsified report, and offers to make it vanish if she pilots the fleet through the Narrows. Beat: the trap of her own buried name—her past weaponized against her.

chapters.title: Refusal at Low Water
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She refuses, and Hale lets the Marrow's mooring lines be cut and her fuel sabotaged—deniable, quiet, professional. Stranded, Sable must choose: report it and lose her window, or fix it herself and run the Narrows alone with Ilsa. Beat: humiliation transmuted into defiance.

chapters.title: Night Work
chapters.summary: Sable and Ilsa's alternating POV. They siphon, patch, and rig repairs by lantern light while the fleet's generators hum across the channel. Ilsa proves useful—she can read the survey data that shows a deep channel the charts don't record. Beat: two guarded women becoming a crew.

chapters.title: The First Tide
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She runs the lower Narrows at first light, threading water the fleet must wait to sound. Behind her, Hale's barges follow her wake exactly—she's become their pilot whether she likes it or not. Beat: the bitter irony of leading your hunters.

chapters.title: Ansen's Cache
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Following Ansen's coded field notes, Ilsa locates a cache on a gravel bar: the full sonar survey, plus Ansen's journal naming the fleet's backer—a former dam administrator whose career was built on the flood. Beat: proof in hand, and the weight of what proof costs.

chapters.title: The Middle Reach
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The river turns hostile: a shifting bar where the old charts and the new survey disagree. Sable grounds the Marrow briefly, frees her, and realizes the fleet is closing the gap—Hale has hired a local pilot who knows her old tricks. Beat: the advantage eroding.

chapters.title: The Pilot Who Knew Her
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The fleet's new pilot is Dree Callas, Sable's former deckhand and the only person alive who knows her old routes. Dree signals her across the water: she doesn't believe the stories about Sable, but she needs paying. Beat: loyalty tested against survival—Dree's, and Sable's faith in it.

chapters.title: The Calving
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The glacier calves early and violently; the route begins to close from the top. The fleet loses its lead barge to ice, and Hale's careful menace cracks into open ruthlessness—he radios an order Sable intercepts: take the survey woman, sink the boat. Beat: the race becomes a hunt.

chapters.title: Kettle Landing
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Sable and Ilsa reach the drowned town at slack water: rooftops under green ice-melt, the old church steeple breaking the surface. Ansen is there—alive, hiding in the bell tower, half-mad with the truth he's carried. Beat: awe and dread in equal measure; the past physically risen.

chapters.title: The Man Who Flooded It
chapters.summary: Ansen's POV, told to Sable and Ilsa. The backer, Wray Odell, didn't just flood the town—he drowned the resisters and buried the survey that proved it. The salvage fleet isn't after treasure; it's erasing the last evidence before the river shifts and exposes the town permanently. Beat: the full horror named.

chapters.title: Hale at the Narrows
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Hale's remaining barge forces the closing gap and boards the Marrow at the church shallows. In the fight, Dree Callas turns her wheel hard and blocks the channel behind Hale, choosing Sable over the paycheck. Beat: loyalty answered; the climax ignites.

chapters.title: The Last Tide
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. With ice raining into the Narrows, Sable runs the Marrow downriver through water no one has ever run, carrying Ansen, Ilsa, and the evidence, while the fleet's barge is caught and crushed by the closing ice. Hale goes down with his orders. Beat: the climax—skill, luck, and every debt called in.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, then hearing-room scene. Sable signs her testimony under her real name, surrendering the pen name of her old life, and the falsified report from twelve years ago is overturned alongside Odell's exposure. Beat: truth costing everything she built to hide behind, and being worth it.

chapters.title: The Wreck Stays
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The government moves to preserve Kettle Landing as a protected site; Ilsa is offered the lead on the memorial survey and takes it. Dree signs on as Sable's deckhand. Beat: grief given a shape—names on a stone above water at last.

chapters.title: Her Own Route
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Spring opens the river; the Marrow runs cargo again, but Sable now files a route, keeps a mooring, and lets people know where she is. She measures life in years now, not miles, and finds the accounting survivable. Beat: resolution—identity claimed, the current still carrying her forward.
